title: Telemetry proxy: structured envelope harmonizer and trace-affinity resolver
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Problem: multiple edge producers emit heterogeneous JSON envelopes (different field shapes, tenant keys, trace formats) which causes downstream sinks (Loki, ES) to lose correlation fidelity and inflates costs due to duplicate indexing. We need an intake-side harmonizer that normalizes envelopes, preserves strong correlation/trace affinity, and applies deterministic routing/backpressure so downstream storage is consistent and cost-predictable.

Objectives:
- Define a stable 'structured envelope' canonical mapping that all edge shims and sidecars can normalize to.
- Ensure a single authoritative correlation key (corr_id) is deterministically derived and propagated to spans and log entries.
- Implement a Trace-Affinity Resolver that groups streaming lines into buckets with sticky fanout to downstream partitioning to preserve ordering and reduce cross-shard joins.
- Provide adaptive backpressure/rate-limiting at proxy layer with tenant-priority signals.
- Emit clear observability (metrics/traces) for each step so we can measure origin fidelity and the effectiveness of dedup/aggregation.

Non-goals: full semantic log parsing or long-term storage retention policy changes (handled in storage teams).

Design summary:
- Intake proxy accepts multi-format JSON and protobuf; negotiates schema version via header X-Env-Schema or attempts heuristic detection.
- Normalizer maps incoming fields to canonical envelope fields: timestamp_iso, tenant_id, corr_id (derived), span_refs (OTEL-style), level, payload.{json/string}, tags.{k:v}. Mapping rules and confidence score emitted as meta.trace_hints.
- Corr_id derivation order: 1) explicit corr_id header; 2) otel.trace_id if present; 3) hash(tenant_id + producer_instance + first_non-null_message_field) as fallback. We record derivation_method metric.
- Trace-Affinity Resolver: compute affinity_key = sha1(corr_id || tenant_shard) and assign to routing_bucket = affinity_key % N_buckets. Buckets map to downstream writer partitions to preserve append-order within a bucket. Resolver maintains ephemeral in-memory sticky map for short-lived session affinity to reduce rehash churn.
- Backpressure & rate-limiting: per-tenant token-bucket + global soft-shed thresholds. Slow-path writes are buffered to memory-backed ring and exposed to the console metrics. We support backpressure advisory response (HTTP 429 + Retry-After) for upstream shims and eventual buffered write for non-blocking producers.
- Downstream mappings: Loki writer uses label set {tenant, routing_bucket, level, corr_id_exists} and places raw payload into line field. ES writer indexes canonical fields with corr_id as join key and adds _meta.normalizer_confidence.

Telemetry and health signals:
- Metrics: normalizer_confidence_histogram, corrid_derivation_counter{method}, bucket_assignments_gauge, buffer_fill_ratio{tenant}, proxy_429s_total, per-tenant_latency_p50/p95/p99.
- Traces: each envelope gets a short proxy-span with events for schema_detection, normalization, routing_decision, downstream_handshake. Failures include full stack traces.

Migration plan:
1) Deploy harmonizer in passive mode (no blocking) in edge region A; it emits normalized envelopes in a sidechannel to a 'shadow-loki' index for comparison.
2) Run comparator job for 2 weeks to measure corr_id preservation, duplication, and ordering delta.
3) Activate active routing with small tenant opt-in (5 tenants) and monitor for regressions.
4) Gradually increase traffic, flipping on backpressure policies after observed stability.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Memory vs disk buffering: prefer in-memory for latency but will fall back to disk-based ring for heavy bursts. Need infra ops approval for the disk option.
- Number of routing buckets (N_buckets) — trade-off between ordering fidelity and shard skew. Proposal: start with power-of-two 256 and adjust via telemetry.
- Legacy consumers that expect unnormalized payloads: we will continue offering passthrough mode behind a smaller port for backward compatibility.

- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Telemetry+Proxy+Envelope+Design

- Comparator dashboard (shadow vs live): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/ingest-shadow-compare
- RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ExampleRFC

Acceptance criteria:
- Normalizer runs in passive mode for all incoming traffic for 2 weeks with confidence >= 0.85 for 90% of envelopes.
- Trace-affinity buckets prevent cross-bucket reorder > 0.1% on opt-in tenants.
- No customer-visible 5xx increase during opt-in phase.

Implementation notes:
- New module: ingest/proxy/harmonizer in Go (reuse existing serde libs).
- Use existing tenant-shard service for tenant->shard mapping.
- Add unit and integration tests: sample producer fakes, shadow comparator job, chaos test for sticky map rebuild.
